title: Begin with the goal
summary: Plan a small school library service. Name the users, their main task, the data, and a clear goal before choosing any tools.
introduction: Before building a tree house, you draw a plan. You decide who will use it, how big it should be, and how to keep it steady. System design does the same kind of planning for an app.
learningObjectives: Name the main parts of a small service
Keep a first version focused on one useful task

blocks.text: **System design** is planning how parts of a service work together. A service does a useful job, such as finding a library book. The plan includes data, requests, speed, cost, and what happens when a part stops working.

A **client** is the part a person uses, such as a web page. A **server** is a program that handles requests from clients. A **database** stores organized information so it can be found and changed later.

Think of a library desk. A learner asks for a book, a librarian checks the catalog, and the learner gets an answer. In our plan, the web page asks the service, and the service checks stored book records.

We will learn with paper plans, tiny calculations, and small browser examples. You do not need a cloud account or a running server to follow this course. The plans describe systems you could build later.

items: Name the users: learners looking for books and a librarian who updates the catalog.
Pick one first task: search by title and see the shelf for each matching copy.
List the needed facts: book ID, title, copy ID, and shelf.
Set a goal we can check: at least 95 of every 100 searches finish within 2 seconds during the expected busy period.
Leave payments and video lessons out of this first version.

blocks.code:
First version: school book search
Users: learners and one librarian
Input: part of a book title
Work: find matching books and their copies
Reply: titles and shelf labels
Goal: 95 of 100 searches finish within 2 seconds
Not included: payments or video lessons
blocks.title: Begin with the goal example

blocks.text: This small plan tells us what to build and what to leave out. We can begin with one app and one database, then measure whether they meet the goal.
A drawing is only one part of the design. Write down why each box is needed. Also explain which data moves between the boxes and what a person sees if a request fails.
A bigger design is not always a better design. More parts can help with growth, but they also create more connections to test and repair.
A goal is not a result yet. We must test the finished service with realistic work. If we do not know how busy the school is, write an estimate and label it as an assumption.

items: Plan a lunch menu app. Write one user, one input, one reply, and one thing you will leave out.
One possible answer: learners choose a day and receive that day's menu. Leave food payments out of the first version.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not choose many tools before you know the problem. Start with the user task and a goal you can check.
